title: Gas exchange system labelling sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Muscles and bones (7C); the particle model (7G)
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 17 (Gas exchange system labelling sheet (portal worksheet, printable or on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 17: Breathing: the gas exchange system. To understand how the organs of the gas exchange system move air into and out of the lungs

picture.alt: A diagram of the human gas exchange system
picture.draw: Draw and label: Gas exchange system labelling sheet

questions.q: Put in order: bronchioles, trachea, alveoli, bronchi.
questions.model: Start at the widest tube: trachea. It splits into bronchi. Bronchi branch into bronchioles. They end in tiny sacs: alveoli.

questions.q: How much more carbon dioxide is in exhaled air than inhaled air (use the table)?

questions.a: They sweep mucus, dust and germs up out of the airways.

questions.q: Core: Label a diagram of the gas exchange system with the five key words and one job for each (portal worksheet).
questions.a: Trachea: carries air; bronchi: into each lung; bronchioles: spread air through the lung; alveoli: gas exchange; lungs: organs of breathing.
questions.model: Teacher labels the trachea first: 'Trachea: tube held open by rings of cartilage, carries air to the bronchi.'

questions.q: Extend: Explain why breathing and respiration are different. Write in the portal response box. Start: 'Breathing is ... whereas respiration is ...'
questions.a: Breathing is moving air in and out of the lungs, whereas respiration is a chemical reaction in cells that releases energy from glucose.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why smokers often cough in the morning.
questions.a: Smoke damages cilia, so mucus is not swept away overnight and must be coughed up.

questions.q: Big question: what happens to the air you breathe in?
questions.a: It travels down the trachea, bronchi and bronchioles to the alveoli, where oxygen passes into the blood.
